executiveSummary: GM0267 passes the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract and has a coherent 2025 administrative base: 45,720 residents, 33 neighbourhoods in five districts, three BAG places, seventeen settlement labels, one ProRail station, 38 scheduled-transit stop areas and seven logical A28/N301/N303/N798/N806 links. Neighbourhood rows reconcile exactly to the municipality population control, while rounded and null cells retain source semantics. Operational release is nevertheless correction-required. Nijkerk spans the low, subsided peat-and-clay Arkemheen polders beside Eemmeer/Nijkerkernauw, the Arkervaart/industrial harbour and the transition toward wooded Veluwe landscapes. Rijkswaterstaat classifies Nijkerkernauw as a Randmeer bounded by Nijkerkersluis, while provincial evidence identifies A28 as the city-polder edge and N301/Nijkerkerbridge as the cross-water Flevoland corridor. The model instead emits a generic river-flood scalar of 0.864490 through T+72, 11,481 affected resident-equivalents and 1,030,949.215 deprived person-hours without a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel branch, Randmeer level, Nijkerkersluis/Arkemheen defence or pump state, breach, hydraulic grid, arrival or recession. Eight active T+24 presets reuse one neighbourhood order led by Spoorkamp/De Terrassen and Hoevelaken-Oranjebuurt-Horstbeek rather than differentiating low-polder hydraulics, rain/drainage, urban heat, Veluwe-edge fire/smoke, cyber targets and industrial exposure. Public layers add 163 water structures, one RWZI, 61 antenna sites, 44 education locations and one Liander capacity-planning sample; none proves live continuity, backup or restoration. No acute-care facility, KNMI observation, PM2.5 monitor or Waterinfo point is assigned inside the boundary. First-72-hour defence/pump/lock, evacuation, N301 bridge/A28/rail access, external-care, wildfire, water-quality and household-support decisions are absent. Unknown, NoData, catalogue no-match and static/planning values are never zero, dry, safe, open, operational or recovered.

identity.summary: Official 2025 identity, regional assignment, boundary and centre agree.
notes: Feature, bundle and manifest all identify GM0267 Nijkerk in Gelderland and Gelderland-Midden.
The centre 5.5140588, 52.2128421 lies inside the generalized boundary.

geography.summary: Administrative geometry is coherent but cannot represent Randmeer, polder, defence, drainage or fire mechanisms.
notes: Nijkerk spans low Arkemheen polders, Randmeren/Arkervaart and higher wooded eastern landscapes.
Generalized polygons do not encode Nijkerkersluis, Zeedijk/kades, defended side, pump catchments, subsidence, terrain, fuels or route intersections.

demography.summary: The municipality control and rounded neighbourhood rows reconcile exactly.
notes: Official and summed neighbourhood population both equal 45,720; households sum to 18,810 and age-65-plus residents to 9,160.
Exact reconciliation does not remove rounding/suppression; null cells remain Unknown and residents do not equal incident-time occupants.

regionalDetail.summary: Thirty-three neighbourhoods provide useful context but retain gaps and no hazard/utility calibration.
notes: Most statistics cover 31-33 rows; district-heating and public-charging fields are null in all 33.
Water, antenna, education and electricity features are context with affectsSimulation=false and cannot establish current continuity.

settlements.summary: Three BAG places and seventeen BRT settlement labels are coherent.
notes: Hoevelaken, Nijkerk and Nijkerkerveen are the BAG places; labels add four woonkernen, ten buurtschappen and three gehuchten.
Labels do not establish incident-time people in farms, nature, industry, schools, station or recreation areas.

transport.summary: Corridor identity is plausible but event-valid bridge, rail and destination access is unknown.
notes: A28 is the main north-south spine; N301 crosses Nijkerkerbridge toward Zeewolde and N806/N303/N798 serve other neighbours.
Nijkerk station and 38 stop areas are static/scheduled context; no closure, direction, hazard intersection, accessible capacity or external-care destination is selected.

emergencyContext.summary: Regional risk and 72-hour public guidance exist, but action-ready local state/capacity remains unverified.
notes: VGGM prioritises flood, nature fire, cyber and utility disruption; Nijkerk explicitly promotes 72-hour household preparation.
No acute-care facility or observation point lies inside; no support-point network, operator state, fire perimeter, flood boundary or destination capacity is exposed.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at six checkpoints across eight services.
notes: Initial focused audit:model passed two tests.
Inline reproduction captured every preset at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and a controlled local fire without a scratch file.
Outputs are synthetic exercise indices, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, determinism, allocation, reconciliation, ledgers and burden accounting pass.
notes: Availability remains in [0,1], outputs are finite/non-negative, zero-event behavior is exact and burden is monotone.
All services allocate 33 neighbourhoods and reconcile to 45,720; layer choice does not mutate the scenario.
Arithmetic correctness does not validate physical mechanisms, access, actions or recovery.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A false-major-river scalar and common cross-hazard order contradict Nijkerk's geography.
notes: River internal floodDepthM is 0.864490 at T+24/T+72 without a named major river or Randmeer/defence event.
Storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share the same first eight neighbourhoods at T+24.
Low Arkemheen hydraulics, urban heat, Veluwe-edge fuels/smoke and cyber/industrial targets require different evidence surfaces.
Canonical wildfire has direct flame 0.100896 and smoke 0.373948 but uses the same generic order.

serviceDependencies.summary: Polder water control, bridge/rail access, external care and utilities are absent or synthetic.
notes: 163 water assets do not form an approved defence-kade-pump-ditch-sewer-RWZI graph or influence recovery.
Roads affect mobility/supply only but lack event passability; N301 bridge, rail, care destinations and nature access have no operational state.
Liander sample, antennas, schools and external hospitals provide context, not continuity, backup, occupancy or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers close, but selected public events and accountable actions are absent.
notes: No Randmeer level/forecast, defence/lock/pump state, rain event, fire perimeter/risk phase, route/rail status, facility or operator incident is selected.
Flood/fire/outage response lacks owner, trigger, request, decision, resources, dependencies, execution, verification, uncertainty and rollback.
First-72-hour actions need warning, evacuation/shelter, pump/lock/road decisions, external care, vulnerable-person support, communications and re-entry.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound plateaus and exact clearing lack local milestones.
notes: River T+72 retains scalar 0.864490, severity 0.267703, 11,481 affected and 1,030,949.215 person-hours; every service equals T+24 exactly.
Compound T+72 retains scalar 0.422802, severity 0.497132, 26,970 affected and 1,876,067.542 person-hours with near-exact service plateaus.
Pluvial and wildfire forcing become exact zero without verified drainage/fire, access, utility, care or public-health milestones.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity and population controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0267 identity, centre, province and safety region agree; 33 neighbourhood rows reconcile exactly to 45,720 residents.
findings.action: Retain source edition, rounding/suppression and Unknown semantics; never infer incident occupancy from exact reconciliation.

findings.summary: The river preset creates unsupported major-river inundation in a Randmeren/polder municipality.
findings.evidence: The scalar is 0.864490 through T+72 with 11,481 affected and 1,030,949.215 person-hours, but no Rhine/Meuse/IJssel branch, Randmeer level, Nijkerkersluis/Arkemheen defence or pump state, breach, grid, arrival or recession is selected.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing river depth/exposure/recovery. Add a distinct authority-selected Randmeer/polder event; unselected cells remain Unknown, not dry.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse one neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all start with Spoorkamp/De Terrassen, Hoevelaken-Oranjebuurt-Horstbeek, De Flier/Arkerpoort and Slichtenhorst in the same order.
findings.action: Replace the common seed with hazard-specific physical surfaces/targets and preserve unsupported cells as Unknown.

findings.summary: Arkemheen defence, ditch, pump, sluice and RWZI context is visible but non-causal.
findings.evidence: HWH assigns 163 structures, including Nijkerk/Hertog Reijnout/Watergoor pumps, three sluices and an RWZI; WV inspects 280 km of Arkemheen ditches. No approved connectivity, compatible capacity, state, power/backup, catchment or recovery edge exists.
findings.action: Build authority-approved non-sensitive compartments and defence-kade-pump-ditch-sewer-RWZI dependencies, retaining missing/sensitive state as Unknown.

findings.summary: Rain, groundwater, subsidence, drought and water-quality mechanisms lack governing evidence.
findings.evidence: Arkemheen is low peat/clay polder terrain with subsidence and managed ditches. The pluvial scalar is 0.409513 at T+24 then zero at T+72 without hyetograph, DEM, initial ground/surface-water level, ditch/sewer/pump state or intervention edition.
findings.action: Integrate the governing stress-test/terrain/groundwater/sewer-surface-water evidence and explicit water-quality/drought observations with issue/valid time and NoData.

findings.summary: Veluwe-edge wildfire/smoke uses generic proximity and neighbourhood allocation.
findings.evidence: Canonical T+24 flame is 0.100896 and smoke 0.373948 with 480 affected; a controlled eastern fire gives flame 0.258354/smoke 0.400140 and 3,764 affected, yet both retain the cross-hazard ranking without fuel, perimeter, access, vulnerable sites or response-water evidence.
findings.action: Require eligible vegetation, fire perimeter/risk phase, weather/spread/smoke, exposed objects/people, access/water and incident-command evidence.

findings.summary: N301 bridge/A28/rail and external acute-care dependencies cannot influence decisions.
findings.evidence: N301/Nijkerkerbridge is the direct Flevoland link and A28 the main spine; Nijkerk station is inside. No RIVM SEH lies inside; nearest records are Amersfoort and Harderwijk. No closure, hazard intersection, referral, destination status or accessible capacity is selected.
findings.action: Add event-valid direction-aware routes to external care, shelters, support points, water/utility sites and fire access without inventing throughput from static maps/schedules.

findings.summary: Utility planning and 72-hour advice do not establish incident continuity or support.
findings.evidence: The Liander sample reports queues/projects but not topology/load/outage; antenna and school registers lack backup/roles. Nijkerk advises 72-hour kits and warns digital alerts can fail, but the model has no support-point, distribution, communications fallback or household-reach state.
findings.action: Use operator/authority-approved aggregate incident/restoration bands and accountable support/distribution/communications actions; planning/advice remains context.

findings.summary: No local KNMI, PM2.5 or Waterinfo point supports exact local event values.
findings.evidence: The current scoped public extracts assign zero KNMI weather stations, RIVM PM2.5 stations, Waterinfo observations and Waterinfo forecasts to GM0267. That is a coverage gap, not observed zero weather, smoke or water hazard.
findings.action: Expose coverage/nearest-point limits and require governed interpolation or event boundaries with publisher, units, issue/valid time, uncertainty and licence.

findings.summary: Exact T+24-72 river/service plateaus and hazard clearing lack verified milestones.
findings.evidence: Every river service is identical from T+24 to T+72 while burden quadruples; compound services nearly plateau; pluvial/fire forcing clears to exact zero without pump/ditch/fire/route/utility/care verification.
findings.action: Replace exact transitions with uncertainty envelopes and owner-verified milestones for water control, fire all-clear, access, utilities, care, support and re-entry.

findings.summary: Coastal, earthquake and cyber outputs are synthetic scope statements, not all-clear conclusions.
findings.evidence: Coastal direct inundation is zero while Randmeer water/wind pathways differ; earthquake is direct-zero with residual burden; cyber has no selected target. No current local observation or incident is bound.
findings.action: Keep direct-versus-indirect and synthetic labels; add events only with source, time, geometry/target, units, uncertainty, coverage, licence and NoData.

findings.summary: The complete numerical and coverage contract passes.
findings.evidence: Ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services are finite/deterministic; no-event behavior, allocation, totals, ledgers, burden and layer invariance pass.
findings.action: Keep GM0267 in regression and add false-major-river, hazard-specific allocation, water-system, access and Unknown-versus-zero assertions.

corrections.validation: Require named Randmeer/Nijkerkernauw level/forecast and datum, Nijkerkersluis/defence/pump state, breach/overtopping/closure case, protected side, connected depth/velocity/arrival/recession grid, issue/valid time, probability/uncertainty, resolution, coverage, NoData and licence. corrections.validation: Use hydraulic/rain-flow cells for flood, shade/building/vulnerability for heat, eligible vegetation/perimeter/plume for fire/smoke and asset targets for cyber. Assert unrelated active hazards cannot share a full rank order; unsupported cells remain Unknown.

corrections.summary: Build a current safe aggregate Arkemheen defence-pump-ditch-sewer-RWZI graph and version rain/groundwater/drought evidence.
corrections.validation: Reconcile WV/HWH/RWS objects into authority-approved compartments with compatible units/current states, power/backup and uncertainty. Obtain governing rain raster/hyetograph, DEM/intervention, ground/surface-water and sewer assumptions. Tests reject automatic dry/recovered where evidence is absent.

corrections.summary: Add event-valid N301 bridge/A28/rail, external-care and fire-response access.
corrections.validation: Use NWB/NDW, RWS/Province, ProRail/operators, GHOR/RIVM and neighbours. Intersect selected hazards with N301/Nijkerkerbridge, A28/N-roads, rail, fire/water access and Amersfoort/Harderwijk care. Record direction, issue/valid time, accessibility, destination and Unknown capacity; static records never prove operation.

corrections.summary: Add safe aggregate utility and first-72-hour support dependencies while preserving observation gaps.
corrections.validation: Use Liander/Vitens/telecom, municipality and VGGM approved zones/restoration bands. Planning queues never imply outage or priority. Add owner/trigger/execution/verification for support points, vulnerable-person reach, water/food/cash distribution and communications fallback. Zero assigned monitoring points display coverage NoData, never safe/zero.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, route guarantee or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed even where sums reconcile exactly; null operational, monitoring, facility or forecast fields are Unknown, not zero.
Generalized boundaries are unsuitable for dike, hydraulic, rain, groundwater, sewer, terrain, vegetation, building, asset or route intersections.
Arkemheen landscape/nature and historic flood evidence is not a current defence assessment, water level, breach, pump state or hydraulic run.
Nijkerkernauw/Nijkerkersluis identity does not establish live level, gate/lock integrity, navigation, flood protection or maintenance completion.
No selected RWS/Waterinfo or water-board event footprint, boundary condition, defence state, arrival/recession grid or probability is consumed.
No complete local rain hyetograph, stress-test raster, DEM/intervention edition, groundwater state, sewer/ditch model or pump state is consumed.
HWH's 163 assigned records have partial coverage and source-specific capacities; register presence/status is not connectivity, operation, backup or restoration.
Current bagging/inspection pages are work and maintenance context, not proof of completed conveyance or present incident capacity.
No KNMI, RIVM PM2.5 or Waterinfo point lies inside GM0267; absence is coverage NoData, not zero weather, smoke or water hazard.
NWB/NDW, GTFS and ProRail data do not establish live road/bridge/rail passability, direction, accessibility, emergency throughput or destination access.
No RIVM acute-care record lies inside GM0267; external hospital records do not establish referral, occupancy, staffing, diversion, generator endurance or access.
DUO and RDI records identify static locations/applications, not people present, shelter role, coverage, backhaul, power/backup, damage or restoration.
One NBNL sample is large-user planning context, not municipal coverage, current load, switching, outage, reserve or restoration.
Municipal 72-hour guidance does not prove household preparation, support-point staffing, communications, stocks, capacity or endurance.
Registered residents exclude incident-time visitors, industry/workplaces, station passengers, schools, farms, nature/recreation sites and livestock.
Direct coastal/earthquake zero is a narrow model statement, not absence of Randmeer/wind, seismic, industrial, access or supply effects.
Recovery beyond T+72, warning lead, mutual aid, shelter/care capacity, public health and long-term re-entry remain outside locally validated scope.

GM0267-POLDER-WATER-001 and GM0267-PLUVIAL-DROUGHT-001 — WV, municipality, HWH and RWS should reconcile defence/pump/ditch/sewer/RWZI and rain/groundwater/drought evidence without invented connectivity.

GM0267-ACCESS-CARE-001 — RWS/NDW, Provinces Gelderland/Flevoland/Utrecht, ProRail/operators, GHOR and neighbours should review event-valid N301 bridge/A28/rail and external-care access without invented throughput.
